item.description: WWE CM Punk’s time as an active WWE wrestler may be closer to an end than fans thought after a big rumor about a new backstage role inside the company. There were many who doubted Punk was capable of having a successful second run in WWE. He left over a decade ago on really bad terms, then when he returned to the industry with AEW five years ago — after many years away from it — that relationship also ended poorly. Including a couple of backstage fights. However, three years after his shocking return at Survivor Series 2023, all reports since suggest the WWE legend is a beloved member of the roster. He is willing to do whatever it takes to promote the brand and impart his wisdom on younger stars. It has created an unexpected bond between him and the company’s head of creative, Triple H, after the two butted heads years ago. Well, it seems that the trust and admiration that WWE decision-makers have for CM Punk is so strong that he is allegedly being eyed for a major backstage role. According to PW Insider, Punk is in the early stages of training to be Shawn Michaels’ replacement in NXT. The outlet reported last month that Michaels is expected to replace retiring WWE executive Bruce Pritchard next year. In Friday’s story, they noted that the Hall of Famer will soon start “splitting his time between NXT and WWE HQ to prepare for that transition.” It is why they claim “Punk has been at the majority of WWE NXT broadcasts in recent weeks alongside Michaels and is currently being prepped for that role.” CM Punk is an inspired choice to take over NXT The PW Insider report notes that there is no clear timeline on when Punk would bring his in-ring career to a close since “the company wants everyone involved to take time to ensure it’s the right fit for all involved.” Nevertheless, they want him to be the man to guide NXT into the future. Most assumed the 48-year-old would try to compete into his 50s. Especially since he is currently in the best shape of his career and doesn’t have the same mileage as most stars his age because he was away from the business for a decade. The idea of him retiring soon will surely disappoint many WWE fans since several other greats have ended their careers over the last few years. However, of the potential options to lead NXT, Punk is a fascinating choice. Obviously, he does not have experience running a promotion and TV show. But neither did Michaels, and he has done a very good job in the role. Besides that, the future Hall of Famer has done a lot in the wrestling industry and can offer a ton of valuable advice to prospects. item.title: UTSA, basketball coach Austin Claunch part ways following DWI arrest
item.description: UTSA men's basketball coach Austin Claunch, center, watches his team during practice at the new Basketball & Volleyball Training Center in San Antonio on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) UTSA and men's basketball coach Austin Claunch have mutually agreed to part ways, Roadrunners athletics director Lisa Campos announced Friday, ending his tenure after two seasons in the wake of an arrest on suspicion of DWI . Acting head coach Nick Bowman, a longtime Claunch assistant, will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season after leading the Roadrunners to a 2-1 start. Austin Claunch, 36, is pictured in a mugshot at the Nueces County jail. He is charged with driving while intoxicated. (Courtesy of the Corpus Christi Police Department) "After thoughtful discussions about the future of the program, we mutually agreed that this was the right time for a transition," Campos said in a statement. "We thank Coach Claunch for his efforts over the last two years and wish him nothing but the best in the future. We look forward to this season with Nick Bowman at the helm." Less than a week before the start of the season, Claunch was found passed out behind the wheel of his Mercedes-Benz 350 Series at 2 a.m. on Oct. 27 in a Stripes parking lot in Corpus Christi, per the arrest report. The report from the Corpus Christi police department states that officers found Claunch unconscious, wearing his seatbelt with the vehicle running and the door left open. The initial call to law enforcement said Claunch had been "stumbling around" the store, and he responded with thick, slurred speech when the officers woke him. He admitted that he had been drinking and drove himself to the Stripes store, and he performed poorly on the field sobriety tests , per the arrest report. He refused blood and breath tests, and he was transported to an area hospital. His suspension was announced the next day, and the Roadrunners opened the season under Bowman's leadership on Nov. 2. "I want to thank our players, staff, administration, and fans for the support they've shown me during my time at UTSA," Claunch said in a statement Friday. "Dr. Campos and I agreed that it was best for both sides to move in a different direction. I want to thank Dr. Campos for the opportunity to coach at UTSA. I'll always be rooting for UTSA and the young men in this program." Because Claunch and UTSA mutually agreed to part ways, neither side is owed a buyout or any financial compensation, per a UTSA spokesperson. Claunch was hired in April 2024 on a five-year contract that ran through the 2028-29 season at an annual guaranteed compensation $550,000, and Claunch would have been owed 65% of his remaining guaranteed compensation if UTSA fired him without cause. Bowman came to UTSA as an assistant on Claunch's initial staff in April 2024 following a year as the lead assistant and recruiting coordinator at New Orleans. item.title: Steeler who had Week 3 Burrow strip sack won't face Bengals | Report
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon isn't expected to return from a foot injury to face the Cincinnati Bengals ahead of their NFL Week 10 showdown on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium, according to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Ray Fittipaldo . Harmon hasn't played since suffering a foot injury Oct. 1 against Cleveland. Harmon was considered the Steelers' biggest question mark for Week 10 on the team's injury report . He was designated to return from injured reserve and practiced Thursday and Friday, but was limited. "We'll see by tomorrow," Harmon told reporters after Friday's practice. With 53 seconds left in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers in Pittsburgh in Week 3, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled as he was sacked by Harmon at the Pittsburgh 46-yard line. The ball was recovered by Pittsburgh's Sebastian Joseph-Day at the Cincinnati 49. Harmon beat Bengals offensive lineman Dalton Risner to get to Burrow. "We've got to be better," Burrow said after the game. "… You can't shoot yourself in the foot . Can't win in this league like that." Bengals tight ends Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson were adamant after the game that All recovered Burrow's fumble. All said a Pittsburgh player was just laying on the ball, but it was All who secured it. The call didn't go the Bengals' way. item.title: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026
item.description: Germany U21 1-2 Belgium U21: Di Salvo's depleted side suffer first defeat of 2026 Due to players getting nominated for the senior side by Jürgen Klopp and many injuries, Germany looked very different from the side that played the majority of the qualification campaign for the European championship. However, they had the first two chances with Anton Kade's blocked effort and Paris Brunner's off-target shot. The next five minutes belonged to Belgium as Julian Duranville scored with his second attempt of the game. A minute after his solo effort narrowly missed the target, the former BVB winger had the simplest task of converting a tap-in after Lucas Stassin's cutback. Germany regained control after conceding the opening goal, with Muhammed Damar playing a big part in most of their promising attacks. The Wolfsburg midfielder was also the one who brought the hosts back in Essen twenty minutes before the half-time break. Lucas Noubi's challenge on Brunner gave Germany a free-kick opportunity from close range, which was calmly converted by Damar. The Hoffenheim loanee scored with the brilliant tactic of hitting it under the wall. The 22-year-old last played for Antonio Di Salvo's side a year ago, but he played a starring role in the absence of star names. Belgium's goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans saved his next attempt after a deflection as Damar decided to go alone in a 4 vs. 3 counter-attacking situation. Stassin hit the post with the last meaningful action of the first-half, although Germany were on top for the most part. It was Germany's turn to be denied by three woodwork early after the restart as the “Man of the Hour” Damar hit the crossbar moments before Kade's header narrowly missed the target. Damar and Kade created several promising opportunities in the final third, but they were among the first players to be taken off by Di Salvo. However, it was Belgium's substitute Romeo Vermant who scored within seconds of entering the game. Nicolo Tresoldi's Club Brugge teammate nutmegged Dennis Seimen to put the visitors ahead for the second time in the game. Brunner hit the sidenetting from a promising position before Brughmans made some decent saves to deny substitutes Maurice Krattenmacher and Merit Kömür. Debutant Louey Ben Farhat also came close to leveling the score for the hosts with his first action of the game. Nonetheless, Belgium U21 held on to their slender lead to beat their Germany counterparts for the third time in a row. After eight successive wins in the Euros qualifying campaign, Di Salvo's suffered their first defeat in 2026. Germany U21 will end the year with a friendly against Croatia in Rijeka on Tuesday.

Palma has made seven competitive appearances for Udinese, scoring once, and currently boasts a market value of €8 million (according to Transfermarkt). That makes him one of the most valuable centre-backs in the world born in 2008. Interestingly, Palma is no stranger to German football. The defender came through Hertha BSC's academy before moving to Udinese in 2022. He also represented Germany at U16 and U17 level before opting to play for Italy internationally just recently. Leipzig could certainly use some “fresh blood” at the back. Castello Lukeba is attracting interest from several European heavyweights, while veteran Willi Orban's contract is approaching its expiry. item.title: Aston Martin F1 Problems Persist; Honda Under Pressure
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Three races remain in the 2026 Formula 1 season, and for Aston Martin, the end of this disappointing season can’t come quickly enough. It has been a rough year for the Silverstone-based team, which had high hopes of competing amid the new regulations and the addition of legendary designer Adrian Newey, who took over as team principal. Unfortunately for Aston Martin and the Stroll family, it has been the team’s worst season since returning to the grid in 2021, with only seven points through 20 races. Aston Martin ranks 10th in the Constructors’ Championship, only ahead of Cadillac, which joined the Formula 1 grid as a brand new entrant this year. For many teams, upgrades and developments throughout a season address problems, but throughout the grand prix schedule, they have continued to be plagued with issues and have very few positives to take from the year. Aston Martin’s PU Problems Persist The problems started almost immediately, with the AMR26 suffering severe vibrations that forced Fernando Alonso to retire on Lap 21 of the Australian Grand Prix. Lance Stroll’s car had similar issues, and he eventually finished 15 laps down after limping around for data-gathering purposes. With Newey able to work on improving the aerodynamic side of the car, which ultimately led to a B-spec being introduced at the Hungarian Grand Prix, the main issue has primarily been reliability and power issues with the team’s Honda power unit. The team has struggled for pace all year, regularly finishing towards the back of the grid, and Stroll made recent comments on how much Aston Martin was losing compared to the rest of the field. “We’re really struggling on the engine side. We know that, so a lot of work to be done,” he told reporters before the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. “We’re missing two seconds [a lap] in engines, so it’s difficult.” With Alonso finishing qualifying in Malaysia two seconds behind pole sitter Max Verstappen, Stroll’s comments suggest that there is a lot more the car could offer if Honda’s power unit was on par with its competitors, such as Mercedes, Ferrari, and even Red Bull Powertrains. Throughout the year, Aston Martin have also struggled to see out races largely due to reliability issues, which have seen Alonso retire from seven races and Stroll retire from 13. Such issues have limited what either driver could do, with Alonso claiming all of the team’s points with a season-high P8 coming in Malaysia. Stroll, meanwhile, has had the worst of it and also achieved his best performance in Malaysia with a P12 finish, with just six race finishes. item.title: Estonia latest country to ban Russian athletes
item.description: Estonia shares a border with Russia [Getty Images] Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine. It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements. The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus. In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality". They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military. Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms. However, it has now emerged that Estonia's government has written to the FIS, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from Russia and Belarus would undermine the country's support of Ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda. In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation. "With that said, the Individual Neutral Athlete policy is clear in stating that notwithstanding eligibility, the host country visa and entry policies remain in place and are determined solely by the host country. FIS bears no responsibility for denial of visas or entry to any person granted eligibility under the FIS Individual Neutral Athlete Policy." On Thursday, Scandinavian neighbours Norway and Finland both said they would also block visas for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine. Norway is preparing to host the cross-country skiing World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the figure skating world championships in March. The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland. This comes in the wake of last month's decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to overturn a ban of Russia by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), a move condemned by the British, German, Finnish and Czech federations. Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022, but the Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) then successfully appealed that decision at Cas. item.title: How Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reacted to CFP expansion
item.description: LAWRENCE — Kansas football coach Lance Leipold shared his support for the expansion of the College Football Playoff this past Monday, Nov. 9, following the announcement that the postseason event would be moving to 24 teams with the 2027-28 season. Leipold, whose time in coaching includes competing in playoffs at Division III-level Wisconsin-Whitewater previously in his career, understands there are a lot of components to consider at the Division I level. That includes what’s going to happen with bowl games. But he thinks this can be a good thing for the sport, which currently has a 12-team playoff. Leipold pointed to the NFL and how it’s nowhere near as big a deal if the top team loses a regular-season game there as it is in college. From his perspective, college has to get used to the idea that teams will compete in the playoffs in the future with more losses than they’ve had in the past. It’s the new normal. RELATED: Kansas football coach Lance Leipold reflects on key play from UCF loss “All in all, I think it’s good for opportunities,” Leipold told reporters. “I think it’s great. I think we have to continue to manage the calendar as good as we can, for the sake of the game. But, yeah, I think it’s where it was going and as soon as it went to four, I knew it’d keep going. And will it get to 32? We shall see.” Leipold noted he didn’t think it’d be something that would diminish the regular season, as some have debated, as long as at least two rounds can be played on home fields and there isn’t too much of a turn toward neutral sites. The ability to have some level of home-field advantage as something to play for during the regular season is something he considers to be significant for any team and fan base. Also, the more the playoff expands, the more demand there is on programs and fans to travel and use more financial resources. The 24-team edition of the College Football Playoff is set to have 16 of its 23 games played on campus, with those matchups taking place during the first two rounds. The quarterfinals and semifinals will continue to be played at the College Football Playoff’s bowl partner locations. The first championship game of the 24-team format will be played in New Orleans in 2028. Jordan Guskey covers University of Kansas Athletics at The Topeka Capital-Journal. item.title: Manchester United confirm new head coach ahead of Liverpool clash
item.description: Manchester United confirm new head coach ahead of Liverpool clash Mauricio Pochettino Faces Liverpool Test as Manchester United Reset Begins Manchester United have done what desperate clubs do when results collapse and the table starts to look ugly. They have changed the manager. Mauricio Pochettino is in, Michael Carrick is out, and his first proper problem arrives immediately, Liverpool at Anfield. There is no gentle introduction here. United are 18th, they have eight points from 10 league games, and the numbers under Carrick were heading in one direction. His last game summed it up, a chaotic 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa in which United needed two stoppage-time goals just to scrape a point. Entertaining, maybe. Sustainable, clearly not. Pochettino appointment made at speed United confirmed Pochettino on Friday, one day after Carrick was dismissed. He has signed a deal running until the summer of 2029, with the club reportedly paying around £7.4 million to release him from his contract with the United States national team. The pitch from United is familiar enough. High-intensity football, attacking ideas, young players improving. All well and good, but right now this is about stabilising a side that has won only three of 15 matches in all competitions this season, with just one league victory. Pochettino returns to English football after spells at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea. His CV in England remains respectable rather than glittering. He reached the League Cup and Champions League finals with Tottenham, but did not win either. At Paris Saint-Germain, he did at least collect Ligue 1 and the French Cup. Anfield comes too soon for comfort Timing matters, and for United this timing is awkward. Pochettino will first oversee the United States in Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on November 14 and 17. He then begins officially at Old Trafford on Wednesday, meets the squad, runs training on Thursday and has three days to prepare for Liverpool on Sunday, November 22. That is barely enough time to learn names, never mind install a system. He will have to rely on clarity and simplicity. Organise the team, tighten the distances, stop the chaos. Anything more sophisticated can wait. Carrick exit reflects deeper problems Carrick’s dismissal ends a brief reign that never gained traction. He had taken over in January after Ruben Amorim’s departure and earned a full-time deal after securing Champions League qualification. Since then, the drop has been severe. Fifteen matches into a two-year contract signed in May, he is gone. The only league win came in a 5-2 result against Ipswich on August 30. Everything else left United drifting towards the bottom three. That is why Pochettino has been hired. Not for sentiment, not for long-term theory, but because United need points, structure and credibility, starting at Anfield.

item.title: One single matchup that gives Michigan some hope against Oregon
item.description: Not much has gone right for Michigan this college football season. So little that head coach Kyle Whittingham could suddenly find himself on the chopping block when all is said and done after just one year. Heading into a road test against resurgent Oregon, the Wolverines could be headed for yet more disaster. But one matchup on the field might give them a fighting chance. Strength vs. strength Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola celebrates a touchdown by Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. as the Oregon Ducks face the USC Trojans on Sept. 26, 2026, at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Oregon enters its Saturday showdown as a 10.5-point favorite, but Michigan has one significant matchup advantage that could make this considerably more competitive: its elite pass defense against Oregon’s passing attack. The Wolverines are allowing just 154.8 passing yards per game, ranking fourth nationally. They have also surrendered only eight passing touchdowns this season. For an Oregon offense averaging 285.4 passing yards per game, sitting top 15 in FBS, that represents a credible challenge. Pressure without blitzing Michigan’s defensive front makes this matchup particularly dangerous. The Wolverines have recorded 21 sacks and 53 tackles for loss, demonstrating their ability to disrupt quarterbacks before routes develop. Defensive lineman John Henry Daley leads the team with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. If he consistently wins his individual battles against Oregon’s blockers, quarterback Dylan Raiola could face uncomfortable decisions and hurried throws. That matters because Raiola has thrown for 1,354 yards, 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Protecting that efficiency against Michigan’s pressure will be essential. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 11’s biggest games Numbers favor Michigan’s defense The contrast is striking. Oregon is a potent aerial offense, while Michigan ranks fourth nationally in total defense, surrendering only 255.3 yards per game on average. Michigan also has veteran defensive backs capable of challenging Oregon’s receivers in man coverage. Will that be enough? Almost certainly not, considering Michigan basically can’t move the ball. But the Wolverines’ pass rush and secondary present a legitimate opportunity early on. That could theoretically slow down the Ducks’ aerial attack enough to make it close. item.title: Tiger Woods remembers Dan Hicks after unexpected death: ‘A great friend to me’
item.description: Tiger Woods paid tribute to late NBC Sports golf voice Dan Hicks , calling the longtime broadcaster "a great friend to me both on and off the course" following Hicks' unexpected death at 64. "Dan Hicks was beloved by all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him," Woods said in a statement mourning Hicks, who died Nov. 11 as a result of an acute illness. "His kindness, warmth, and presence will be deeply missed. Like so many in the golf world, Dan was a great friend to me both on and off the course. I had the utmost respect for him and the incredible job he did for our sport for decades." For more than a quarter-century, Hicks was the defining soundtrack to Woods' career, calling 27 of his PGA Tour victories — including Woods' iconic 12-foot birdie putt on the 72nd hole at Torrey Pines to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open , punctuated by Hicks' timeless call: "Expect anything different?" "Our thoughts are with Hannah and their daughters during this incredibly difficult time," Woods added, referring to Hicks' wife, fellow broadcaster Hannah Storm, and their three daughters, Hannah, Ellery, and Riley. "I hope they find comfort in knowing how much he meant to so many people and the lasting impact he made on everyone whose life he touched." View this post on Instagram Storm announced her husband's passing on social media , remembering him as "truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around." Born and raised in Tucson, Arizona, Hicks graduated from Sabino High School and the University of Arizona before starting in local radio and television. After joining CNN in 1989 and moving to NBC Sports in 1992, he worked as a tower announcer until being named lead golf play-by-play voice in 2000. Beyond anchoring NBC's coverage of the U.S. Open, The Open Championship , Ryder Cup, Presidents Cup and FedEx Cup Playoffs, Hicks was a versatile fixture across sports — calling Olympic swimming and skiing, including the U.S. men's freestyle relay comeback at the 2008 Beijing Games, and returning as the lead voice for Notre Dame Football in 2024. Another club legend has unceremoniously been shown the door — the third manager sacked by INEOS in less than two years and three weeks — and the club has confirmed its eighth permanent manager/head coach for the men’s team since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in May 2013. That’s right, Michael Carrick, who took the interim role exactly 11 months ago, coached the team to one of the best second-half of the season records in the Premier League, finished third in the league, and secured Champions League football, is once again forced to take the high road with a classy goodbye post on social media; capping off one final full week of work knowing the ghouls above him were working out the final contract details with another manager whilst he was running training. item.title: DeChambeau Details Plans For New Golf Course In California Hometown
item.description: Bryson DeChambeau has disclosed additional details of the golf course community he's planning in his hometown of Clovis, California. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Images Bryson DeChambeau has partnered with a real estate developer in his hometown of Clovis, California, to create a new residential and lifestyle community called The Orchard Golf Club that pairs championship golf with the region’s rich agricultural heritage. DeChambeau, a two-time U.S. Open champion who attended Clovis East High School and won the California State Junior Championship at age 16, said he feels a “deep responsibility to give back to the region” that has provided him with so much and has been working on regulatory components of the project since 2022. DeChambeau acquired a historic property across the street from his high school, McFarlane Ranch, and is working with Cook Land Company to create the master planned community that will feature an 18-hole golf course and elevated practice facilities. There will also be an on-site farmers market open to the public as well as other community amenities, including programs intended to provide access for kids and schools in the area. “This is a profound opportunity for my team and I to work with the Cook family to help revitalize the area by investing in a project that uses golf to truly serve the community,” DeChambeau said in a press release. DeChambeau said he and his team will design the course and the practice facilities, calling them “the first of many fully procured DeChambeau Designs.” Each hole on the course at The Orchard will be surrounded by a different variety of fruit or nut tree, creating a distinctive experience and highlighting the area’s agricultural ties. A clubhouse and “thoughtfully designed homes” are also part of the plans submitted to the City of Clovis and Fresno County. There is no definitive timetable for the completion of the course or other community components. “The development regulations in California are complex but (the city and county have), and will continue to, work hand in hand to bring this important project to the region,” DeChambeau said in a letter to residents of Clovis, which is about 10 miles northeast of Fresno, and the surrounding Central Valley region. “We anticipate approval within 18 months, with some amenities such as a driving range coming sooner.” A Google Earth image of DeChambeau's high school, Clovis East, and the surrounding area in his California hometown where The Orchard Golf Club is planned.
